description: Cooks every Sunday and keeps making dishes. Studies Japanese on their own, chose a Japanese history elective to understand the culture, watches anime and wants to visit Kyoto. Has three side projects.
tests: When one topic shows up repeatedly across different contexts (self-study, elective class, anime, travel), the topic-level generalization IS allowed. Guards against being so cautious that nothing is promoted
A clear self-statement ("I cook every Sunday... it's my reset") is promoted after one mention
Dishes are appended as separate records, not merged into one sentence
"Yesterday" in a message dated 9/13 is recorded as 9/12
Three projects mentioned once are grouped as records under one projects category; the robot arm's progress is appended

observations.note: She cooks every Sunday and describes vegetable chopping as a way to reset and clear her head.
observations.hook: Using the repetitive act of chopping vegetables as a weekly reset that clears her head.
observations.quote: I cook every Sunday no matter what. It's my reset for the week, chopping vegetables just clears my head.

observations.note: She usually chooses what to cook that same morning based on what is in the fridge.
observations.hook: Choosing what to make in the moment from the ingredients already available.
observations.quote: Usually decide that morning based on whatever's in the fridge.

observations.note: She made shakshuka with eggs poached in spicy tomato sauce, adding cumin and a bit of feta.
observations.quote: I made shakshuka this morning. Eggs poached in spicy tomato sauce, super easy.

observations.note: Made shoyu ramen with chicken from scratch; the broth took seven hours, and the tare was the hardest part.
observations.quote: Made ramen from scratch yesterday. Took me 7 hours for the broth lol

observations.note: Has been learning Japanese with Duolingo for about three months and chose to do so without being asked.
observations.quote: Nobody asked me to learn it, I just wanted to.

observations.note: Read some of the Japanese on a soy sauce label and said they felt proud of doing so.
observations.hook: Putting a practiced skill to use in an everyday setting
observations.caveat: Only some of the label's characters were readable.
observations.quote: I could read the label on the soy sauce bottle. Kinda proud of that.

observations.note: She asked, explicitly beyond the syllabus, how sakoku affected what people ate and whether sushi came from that era. She said she chose the elective to understand the culture behind food and a language she is interested in.
observations.topic: Cultural context of food and language
observations.hook: Understanding the cultural context behind food and language
observations.quote: I picked this elective because I wanted to understand the culture behind the food and the language I'm into.

observations.note: She found it funny that sushi was described as fast food in Edo-era Japan.
observations.hook: The amusing surprise of sushi being framed as fast food
observations.quote: Sushi as fast food is so funny.

observations.note: The student said they felt sad after finishing Frieren; they did not specify what about it they were drawn to.
The student wants to visit Kyoto someday and said anime temple scenes always appeal to them.
observations.hook: Evocative depictions of temples in anime
observations.quote: I really want to go to Kyoto someday, the temple scenes in anime always get me.

observations.note: The student said they are saving up for a possible Kyoto trip next year.
observations.caveat: The trip is tentative; the student said “maybe next year.”
observations.quote: Saving up for it! Maybe next year.
